title: Low-Intensity Focused Ultrasound for Gambling Disorder
official: A Randomized, Sham-Controlled Trial of Low Intensity Focused Ultrasound Neuromodulation as an Adjunctive Treatment for Gambling Disorder
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether low-intensity focused ultrasound (LIFU) is safe and may help reduce gambling-related symptoms in adults seeking treatment for gambling disorder.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Is LIFU safe and well tolerated in adults with gambling disorder?
* Does LIFU reduce gambling behavior compared with a sham (inactive) procedure?

Researchers will compare participants who receive active LIFU with participants who receive sham LIFU to see whether active treatment leads to greater reductions in gambling behavior.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to receive either active LIFU or sham LIFU.
* Receive nine treatment sessions delivered over three treatment days within a five-day period.
* Participate in weekly telehealth cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT).
* Complete assessments of gambling behavior, gambling urges, mood, and quality of life.
* Attend follow-up visits for up to 90 days after active LIFU treatment.

Low-intensity focused ultrasound is a noninvasive technique that uses focused sound waves to influence brain activity. Researchers believe this approach may affect brain circuits involved in reward, cravings, and decision-making that contribute to gambling disorder.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults 18 to 60 years old.
* Currently diagnosed with gambling disorder, confirmed by a clinical interview.
* Seeking treatment for gambling disorder, including people currently participating in or transitioning from addiction treatment programs.
* In generally good enough physical health to safely participate in study procedures.
* Not pregnant and not planning to become pregnant during study participation.
* Able to speak and read English well enough to provide informed consent and complete study assessments.
* Able to safely undergo MRI scans (for example, no metal implants or other conditions that would make MRI unsafe).
* Willing to be randomly assigned to either study group, attend all study visits, and participate in weekly telehealth counseling sessions.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Significant heart, lung, liver, kidney, blood vessel, or blood-clotting problems that may make participation unsafe.
* Unwilling to avoid illegal substance use on study procedure days.
* Currently participating in court-ordered treatment.
* Skin or scalp conditions over the treatment area that may interfere with the study procedure.
* A medical condition that the study doctor believes could increase the risks of the ultrasound procedure, such as a history of seizures, stroke, serious brain injury, or certain brain abnormalities.
* Current or past schizophrenia, another psychotic disorder, or bipolar disorder.
* Diagnosis of a Cluster A or Cluster B personality disorder.
* Unable to safely undergo an MRI scan.
* Pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the study.
* Previous treatment with focused ultrasound neuromodulation or another investigational neuromodulation treatment within the past 90 days.
